title: Later Tang
capsule: The Later Tang (923–936) was the second of the Five Dynasties in post-Tang northern China, founded by Li Cunxu (Emperor Zhuangzong), a Shatuo Turkic warlord who destroyed the Later Liang at the Battle of Yecheng in 923 and claimed restoration of the Tang imperial line. The dynasty reached its greatest extent under Emperor Mingzong (r. 926–933), who was regarded as a relatively capable ruler who stabilised the north and extended Later Tang suzerainty over the Ten Kingdoms of the south. It fell when the Khitan-backed Shi Jingtang revolted in 936, ceded the Sixteen Prefectures (including modern Beijing) to the Khitan Liao dynasty as payment for military support, and founded the Later Jin, ending Later Tang after barely thirteen years.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territory in north China is reconstructed from the Zizhi Tongjian and Five Dynasties history; boundaries with the Khitan Liao and the southern kingdoms shifted rapidly and are modeled with moderate confidence.
